UFS student housing chaos

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Residents of Universitas in Bloemfontein lives have been turned upside down by the student accommodation that has taken over their suburb. Universitas and Brandwag are suburb adjacent to the University which have become an extension of the campus but without the protection of the security and control that university residence do. Retired advocate Neo Sephoti bought a house in Universitas in Bloemfontein in 2005, it was a quite upmarket residential area near University of the Free State and Central University of Technology, but over the last 5 years it has radically transformed. It is now home to 702 student houses, eradicating the residential fabric of the neighbourhood.

Summary:
Neo is very clear that students are desperate for accommodation, and she goes out of her way to welcome them to the community- ensuring she leaves pamphlets in every student house with useful numbers, aware that many of the students are coming from rural areas and need support. But they feel like they are drowning- studentification has caused spatial restructuring and the needs of the student sub-culture dominate. She has no plans to move, but the value of her property has decreased by 60%.

The University has accommodation for 5000 in hostels on campus and the other 20000 students must find accommodation elsewhere. The University has an accreditation process which sets out standards and does inspections but students are still getting exploited. One residence has 56 students on the property, no proper building plans have been passed and there is two toilets and 4 showers for 42 students.

The conflict arises when student life clashes with suburban life and the parties run from Friday night till late Sunday. The police are no longer responding to noise disturbance call outs, its left up to community policing forums or private security. Tensions came to a head in January when residents signed a petition to close down all the student houses. Now the University and the Municipality are meeting with Landlords to try and reach an amicable agreement.

The other issue is the densification of suburbs without the necessary improvement of infra structure. Building plans have not been approved, Sewers are over flowing, rubbish is piling up and spaza shops are popping up in residential areas without business rezoning. NSFAS pays R39700 annually for accommodation and so business is booming. Many of these homeowners don’t live in Bloem and so residents struggle to get them to get the students to comply.

Houses built with single phase electricity and not adapted to accommodate 40 students drawing power are blowing. Universitas residents clean their own streets and sidewalks fully understanding that the Municipality can’t keep up, but they resent having to clean up endless condoms, liquor bottles and their children can no longer play in the parks
As soon as the for-sale sign on a house goes up they bought and the next week the building begins, garages and even the parking areas turned into bedrooms, and backyards into dormitories. The municipality has been conducting inspections - but follow up action of closing them hasn’t happened. The Mungahung Municipality Mayor resigned, there is an acting CFO and there are two building inspectors. Landlords are complaining that even if they try and comply they can't get their plans passed or their businesses certified .

The Municipality has clear bylaws about what a legal student accommodation requires but its overwhelmed. Crime is on the rise and the main targets are the students who are on foot carrying phones and laptops. Neo’s son had his backpack ripped off his back walking home from school.


Further information:
The tension between residential areas adjacent to universities being studentified” is not particular to Bloem, its happening in suburbs across the country near Tertiary institutions. It’s residents and Municipalities that are carrying the burden for lack of Government spending to provide student accommodation. It’s a powder keg. Schalk Schalk van Vuuren, Realtor at Rawson and chair of the Universitas community group is getting death threats from students accommodation homeowners. Students have pelting community policing forums with bottles. But there are many student houses that are quite and well run with no alcohol allowed on the property.

And even although the University says that’s great for local business - it’s wreaking havoc on the residential nature of these areas.
VO 8: Advocate Neo Sephoti moved here 18 years ago - it was supposed to be an investment for her… and her son…but the neighbourhood she bought into - is rapidly changing
Day 1 C0013. 00:00:22:27 Neo: Majority of the houses are turned into student accommodation. …people are buying up and just letting them out

Script: It’s not just established homes being converted.. landlords are cashing in on hastily ..poorly constructed buildings.
Day 1 C0001 00:03:32:25 - Neo “buy property today, tomorrow. They already are advertising for student accommodation. Some of these accommodations that we've been in. The passage is so narrow that God forbid that a fire should break out, those kids would not be able to get out.
VO 10 : SCRIPT: The student boom is affecting all nearby suburbs…Anneke Anker of the Brandwag neighbourhood association, shows us how much new building is taking place. At least a third of homes are occupied by students, and many are badly built.
Day 1 C0042 00:01:40:18 - Anneke: building happens everywhere. And any time, they don't submit building plans and from the Mangaung side, there was delays in building plans. So if your building plan is not approved, you know, you just continue with the building in any way
VO 11 Script: Landlords are taking full advantage of the boom: cramming students into often substandard accommodation. Neo out.00:10:33:17 - we have not seen the municipality coming on board to enforce compliance to building regulations and or even knowing that these plans have been submitted to the municipality.

He’s the Director General of the Free State Education Department, and the owner, of this block of flats built on a residential property. He has shares in several other student digs
Local Councillor Tjaart Van Der Walt claims many buildings aren’t legal - including the one owned by Malakoane.
Day 2 C0004 Tjaart 00:10:03:05 - The building plans weren't approved when it was built, it is still not approved. We even contacted the Public Protector and I spoke to the municipal manager numerous times. …..the owner at the end of the day finished the house and the students started occupying and the house was provisionally accredited by the university.
VO 13 Script “ Adv Malakoane didn’t respond to our email inquiries.
Pause
VO 14 Script: This rapid influx of students could have been better managed if the Municipality had been functioning. But it’s been under NATIONAL administration for the last year and there is a 60% vacancy rate in the planning Department.
Day 2 Cam 2 0030 Link: So the Bloemfontein Mayor has resigned, the City Manager is in an acting position, there are only five building inspectors and the planning department has a backlog, no wonder the landlords are getting away with everything and nothing gets resolved
VO 15 Script: The University is required to INSPECT and accredit student accommodation, before landlords can receive funding, from the National Student Financial Aid Scheme….R45 000 per student per year. Despite residents raising concerns, the majority are only partially accredited, yet STILL get the funding…
Pause
VO 16 Head of Student affairs Themba Hlasho - assured us that landlords who didn’t comply - are deregistered.
Day 1 C0001 00:04:57:24 - Mac: there's a possibility corruption might have have crept in.
Day 1 C000100:05:16:27 Themba: we make sure that we visit those places to ensure that the standard is kept. We also have an off campus officer who actually deals with off accommodation matters.
Day 2 Cam 1C0010 LINK This issue of students, residents, and landlords is not unique to Bloemfontein, But this things took a bit of a nasty turn here in Bloem when 600 residents signed a petition saying students must go
This party, held in the days after our visit, turned violent.
Upsound
17 Script: It’s what Residents are complaining about… and they’re fed up with sitting on the sidelines -
Upsound This became a crime scene now somebody shooting in publice, they taking pictures now
Script: Their petition got the attention of the University, Municipality and the Police.
0:04:27:21 - Anneke: So we need the buy-in from a university. They can't keep on bringing in more students every year if there's no accommodation for them already
VO 18 Script:Inspections have begun, and there is a major showdown looming by the end of April. The Municipality intends to enforce a bylaw - limiting 20 students to 10 rooms per property.
VO 19 It will be chaos - and students will bear the brunt when thousands lose their non-compliant accommodation. We were told to speak to the Municipality’s head of communications - Qondile Khedama - and made an appointment.
LINK Day 2 Cam 2 00.50 Day 2 Cam 2 00.50 So it’s just gone –5pm we have been waiting here since 3.30 waiting for Qondile Khedama, I think it is clear he is not going to meet with us, and nobody from the Municipality is going to account for what is happening.
VO 20 Script: There are no easy solutions. But some - are trying to make things better for everyone.
00:03:50:27 - Neo: If we don't speak up for ourselves and these students, it means people that are not compliant are going to continue doing as they please because they believe that they can….

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Residents of Universitas in Bloemfontein lives have been turned upside down by the student accommodation that has taken over their suburb. Universitas and Brandwag are suburb adjacent to the University which have become an extension of the campus but without the protection of the security and control that university residence do. Retired advocate Neo Sephoti bought a house in Universitas in Bloemfontein in 2005, it was a quite upmarket residential area near University of the Free State and Central University of Technology, but over the last 5 years it has radically transformed. It is now home to 702 student houses, eradicating the residential fabric of the neighbourhood.
metadata.Summary: Neo is very clear that students are desperate for accommodation, and she goes out of her way to welcome them to the community- ensuring she leaves pamphlets in every student house with useful numbers, aware that many of the students are coming from rural areas and need support. But they feel like they are drowning- studentification has caused spatial restructuring and the needs of the student sub-culture dominate. She has no plans to move, but the value of her property has decreased by 60%. The University has accommodation for 5000 in hostels on campus and the other 20000 students must find accommodation elsewhere. The University has an accreditation process which sets out standards and does inspections but students are still getting exploited. One residence has 56 students on the property, no proper building plans have been passed and there is two toilets and 4 showers for 42 students. The conflict arises when student life clashes with suburban life and the parties run from Friday night till late Sunday. The police are no longer responding to noise disturbance call outs, its left up to community policing forums or private security. Tensions came to a head in January when residents signed a petition to close down all the student houses. Now the University and the Municipality are meeting with Landlords to try and reach an amicable agreement. The other issue is the densification of suburbs without the necessary improvement of infra structure. Building plans have not been approved, Sewers are over flowing, rubbish is piling up and spaza shops are popping up in residential areas without business rezoning. NSFAS pays R39700 annually for accommodation and so business is booming. Many of these homeowners don’t live in Bloem and so residents struggle to get them to get the students to comply. Houses built with single phase electricity and not adapted to accommodate 40 students drawing power are blowing. Universitas residents clean their own streets and sidewalks fully understanding that the Municipality can’t keep up, but they resent having to clean up endless condoms, liquor bottles and their children can no longer play in the parks As soon as the for-sale sign on a house goes up they bought and the next week the building begins, garages and even the parking areas turned into bedrooms, and backyards into dormitories. The municipality has been conducting inspections - but follow up action of closing them hasn’t happened. The Mungahung Municipality Mayor resigned, there is an acting CFO and there are two building inspectors. Landlords are complaining that even if they try and comply they can't get their plans passed or their businesses certified . The Municipality has clear bylaws about what a legal student accommodation requires but its overwhelmed. Crime is on the rise and the main targets are the students who are on foot carrying phones and laptops. Neo’s son had his backpack ripped off his back walking home from school.
metadata.Further information: The tension between residential areas adjacent to universities being studentified” is not particular to Bloem, its happening in suburbs across the country near Tertiary institutions. It’s residents and Municipalities that are carrying the burden for lack of Government spending to provide student accommodation. It’s a powder keg. Schalk Schalk van Vuuren, Realtor at Rawson and chair of the Universitas community group is getting death threats from students accommodation homeowners. Students have pelting community policing forums with bottles. But there are many student houses that are quite and well run with no alcohol allowed on the property.
